subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Dizygotic and Monozygotic Twins and Chorionicity

steps.tx: Twins from two separately fertilised eggs are **dizygotic twins**. They are genetically ordinary siblings and always have two placentas, fused or separate. Rising maternal age and assisted conception increase their frequency. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Dizygotic twins come from two eggs and always have two placentas.

steps.tx: Twins from one fertilised egg splitting form **monozygotic twins**. Timing of the split decides chorionicity and amnionicity. Late splits share a placenta and its vascular dangers. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Monozygotic twins split from one egg, and split timing decides their membranes.

nodes.label: Split in first days, two placentas

steps.tx: Whether twins share a placenta, determining surveillance intensity, is **chorionicity**. It is assigned accurately only in the first trimester. Monochorionic twins need fortnightly scans from sixteen weeks for transfusion syndrome. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Chorionicity is assigned in the first trimester and monochorionic twins need fortnightly scans.

steps.tx: A thick membrane insertion with a triangular placental extension is the **lambda sign**. Also called the twin peak sign, it indicates dichorionic twins. Its presence is most reliable before fourteen weeks. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: The lambda or twin peak sign indicates dichorionic twins before fourteen weeks.

steps.tx: A thin membrane meeting the placenta at a right angle without extension is the **T sign**. It marks monochorionic diamniotic twins. These twins share placental vessels beneath their separate sacs. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: The T sign marks monochorionic diamniotic twins sharing placental vessels.

steps.tx: Twins sharing both placenta and amniotic sac are **monochorionic monoamniotic** and rarest. Cord entanglement threatens both twins throughout pregnancy. Planned caesarean at thirty two to thirty four weeks is usual. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Monochorionic monoamniotic twins risk cord entanglement and deliver by planned caesarean early.

steps.tx: Dichorionic twins are watched monthly while monochorionic need fortnightly review, a **surveillance schedule difference**. Growth discordance and fluid imbalance are the targets in monochorionic pairs. Delivery timing also differs by chorionicity. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Surveillance schedules differ, with monochorionic twins scanned fortnightly from sixteen weeks.

steps.tx: Labelling twins consistently as presenting and non presenting across scans prevents errors, termed **twin labelling**. Discordance calculations depend on comparing the same fetus serially. A labelling map in the notes records sac position and sex. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Consistent twin labelling prevents errors in serial growth comparison.

steps.tx: Uncomplicated dichorionic twins deliver around thirty seven weeks and monochorionic around thirty six, following **chorionicity delivery timing**. Monoamniotic pairs deliver earliest by caesarean. These timings balance stillbirth against prematurity. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Delivery timing follows chorionicity, balancing stillbirth against prematurity.
